lessons.title: I have a problem
lessons.scenario: In the laundry room, Sam cannot find his wallet and Mia is worried because she is late.

items.example: Excuse me, I have a problem.
items.note: Say 'I have a problem' when something goes wrong and you need help.

items.example: Hello, Sam! What is wrong?
items.note: Ask 'What is wrong?' when a friend looks sad or worried.

items.example: I cannot pay because I lost my wallet.
items.note: Say 'I lost my wallet' when you cannot find where you put your money and cards.

items.example: I cannot run because I am stuck.
items.note: Say 'I am stuck' when you cannot move or cannot finish what you are doing.

items.example: I must run because I am late for school.
items.note: Say 'I am late' when you arrive after the right time.

items.example: I lost my wallet, so I am worried.
items.note: Say 'I am worried' when you feel nervous about a problem.

grammar.title: I am + feeling or situation
grammar.explanation: Use I am with words like stuck, late, and worried to say what is happening to you right now.
examples: I am stuck behind the door.
I am worried about my wallet.

practice.prompt: You need help because something went wrong. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Use 'I have a problem' to tell someone you need help.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Smarty asks 'What is wrong?' to find out the problem.

practice.prompt: Sam cannot find his money or his bank card. What does he say?
practice.explanation: 'I lost my wallet' means you do not know where your wallet is.

practice.prompt: Match each problem with what it means.
practice.explanation: Match each phrase with the right situation.

practice.prompt: The door will not move. Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I am stuck behind the door.
practice.explanation: Say 'I am stuck' when you cannot get out.

practice.prompt: School starts at eight o'clock, and it is nine o'clock now. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I must run because I am ___.
practice.explanation: When you arrive after the right time, say 'I am late'.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I am worried because I lost my wallet.
practice.answer: I am worried because I lost my wallet.
options: I am worried because I lost my wallet.
I am happy because I found my wallet.
I am tired because I walked home.
practice.explanation: Losing a wallet makes you feel worried.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I have a problem. Can you help me?
practice.answer: I have a problem. Can you help me?
practice.explanation: Use 'I have a problem' before asking for help.

story.hook: Why is Sam worried in the laundry room?

image.describe: In a bright laundry room, Smarty the black cat talks with Sam and Mia near a washing machine while Sam checks his jacket.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Sam! You are not happy. What is wrong?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Smarty, I have a problem. I lost my wallet.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Oh! And I am late for my English lesson!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I am worried because my money and card are in my wallet.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Look! Is that your wallet under the big box?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, it is! My hand is big, so I am stuck behind the box!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I am small. I can get it for you!

questions.prompt: What is Sam's problem?
questions.explanation: Sam says: I have a problem. I lost my wallet.

questions.prompt: Why does Mia have to run?
questions.answer: She is late for her lesson.
options: She is late for her lesson.

questions.answer: Sam is stuck behind the big box.
options: Sam is stuck behind the big box.
Mia is worried about the box.
questions.explanation: Sam says his hand is big, so he is stuck behind the box.

mission.setup: You meet Smarty in the room and tell him what is wrong. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: Hello! You look worried. What is wrong?
turns.hint: Tell Smarty 'I have a problem' or say what happened.

turns.smarty: Tell me more. Did you lose your wallet, or are you late?

lessons.title: Home problems
lessons.canDo: Name things that break at home
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia check broken machines and cleaning tools in the laundry room.

items.example: My dirty shirts are in the washing machine.
items.note: A washing machine cleans your shirts, socks, and trousers with water.

image.describe: a white front-loading washing machine with clean shirts inside

items.example: Be careful with the iron because it is hot.
items.note: An iron gets hot and makes shirts and dresses smooth.

image.describe: a blue electric clothes iron standing on an ironing board

items.example: There is cold water in the yellow bucket.
items.note: Use a bucket to carry water when you clean the room.

image.describe: a yellow plastic cleaning bucket with a handle

items.example: We need a mop to clean the water in the kitchen.
items.note: A mop has a long handle and cleans water off the room.

image.describe: a wooden-handled floor mop with a white cotton head

items.example: Water comes from the tap in the bathroom.
items.note: Turn the tap to start or stop the water in the kitchen or bathroom.

image.describe: a shiny silver water tap over a sink with a drop of water

items.example: This key is for the lock on the front door.
items.note: A lock keeps a door closed until you use the key.

lessons.title: Asking for help
lessons.scenario: Ben needs help using the washing machine and writing a note in the laundry room.

items.example: I do not understand this machine. Could you show me?
items.note: Ask 'Could you show me?' when you want someone to teach you how to do something.

items.example: Sorry, I did not hear you. Could you repeat that?
items.note: Ask 'Could you repeat that?' when you need someone to say something one more time.

items.example: I am getting my key. Could you wait a moment?
items.note: Ask 'Could you wait a moment?' when you need someone to stop for a short time.

items.text: Could you lend me a pen?
items.example: I want to write my name. Could you lend me a pen?
items.note: Ask 'Could you lend me a pen?' when you want to use a pen and give it back later.

items.text: Could you give me a hand?
items.example: This box is very big. Could you give me a hand?
items.note: 'Could you give me a hand?' is a friendly, polite way to ask someone to help you.

items.example: I speak a little English. Could you speak slowly?
items.note: Ask 'Could you speak slowly?' when someone talks too fast for you.

grammar.title: Polite requests with Could you…?
grammar.explanation: Start a question with Could you followed by a base verb to ask someone for help politely.
examples: Could you give me a hand?

practice.prompt: You are carrying a big box and need help. What is a friendly way to ask?
practice.answer: Could you give me a hand?
options: Could you give me a hand?
Could you lend me a pen?
practice.explanation: 'Could you give me a hand?' means 'Could you help me?'

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Ask 'Could you speak slowly?' when someone speaks too fast.

practice.prompt: Match each situation with the best polite question.

pairs.right: Could you lend me a pen?

practice.explanation: Choose the 'Could you…?' question that fits the problem.

practice.prompt: You do not know how to start the washing machine. Build the question.
practice.explanation: Start with 'Could you' and add the base verb 'show'.

practice.prompt: You have a notebook, but nothing to write with. Complete the question.
practice.text: Could you ___ me a pen?
practice.explanation: 'Lend me a pen' means let me use your pen for a short time.

practice.prompt: Your friend is walking away, and you need to tie your shoe. Complete the question.
practice.text: Could you wait a ___?
practice.explanation: 'Wait a moment' means wait for a very short time.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I do not understand. Could you repeat that?
practice.answer: I do not understand. Could you repeat that?
options: I do not understand. Could you repeat that?
I am late. Could you wait a moment?
I have a problem. Could you give me a hand?
practice.explanation: 'Repeat that' means say it again.

practice.prompt: Say the question aloud.
practice.text: Could you give me a hand with the washing machine?
practice.answer: Could you give me a hand with the washing machine?
practice.explanation: Use 'Could you give me a hand…?' to ask politely for help.

lessons.title: Offering help
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Omar see Sam carrying a big bucket and struggling with a stuck lock.

items.example: Do not be worried. I will help you.
items.note: Say 'I will help you' when you decide right now to help someone.

items.example: That bucket is very big. I will carry that.
items.note: Say 'I will carry that' when someone is holding a big or difficult box or bucket.

items.example: Give me the key and I will open it.
items.note: Say 'I will open it' when someone cannot open a door, box, or window.

items.example: The washing machine is broken. Shall I call someone?
items.note: Ask 'Shall I call someone?' to offer to phone a friend, doctor, or mechanic.

items.example: You have three big boxes. Do you need a hand?
items.note: Ask 'Do you need a hand?' to ask politely if someone wants your help.

items.example: You are tired. Let me help with the mop.
items.note: Say 'Let me help' when you step forward to do part of the work.

grammar.title: Offering help: I will, Shall I, Let me
grammar.explanation: Use I will (often shortened to I'll) or Let me to offer help right away, and Shall I…? to ask before you act.
examples: I will carry that for you.

practice.prompt: Omar is carrying a big bucket full of water. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Offer 'I will carry that' when someone is holding a big item.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I will open it for you.
practice.answer: I will open it for you.
options: I will open it for you.
I will carry that for you.
practice.explanation: Say 'I will open it' when a door or box is stuck.

practice.prompt: Match each problem with the best offer of help.
practice.explanation: Choose the offer that solves each problem.

practice.prompt: The washing machine is broken. Offer to phone a mechanic.
practice.explanation: Use 'Shall I call someone?' to offer to phone for help.

practice.prompt: You see Mia working hard in the laundry room. Complete your question.
practice.text: Do you ___ a hand?
practice.explanation: Compare: 'Could you give me a hand?' asks for help; 'Do you need a hand?' offers help.

practice.prompt: Sam cannot clean the water fast. Complete the offer.
practice.text: ___ me help you with the mop.
practice.explanation: Say 'Let me help' to offer to do the work together.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: Do you need a hand? I will help you.
practice.answer: Do you need a hand? I will help you.
practice.explanation: Ask 'Do you need a hand?' and offer 'I will help you.'

lessons.title: If… will…
lessons.scenario: Cloudy weather arrives outside while Smarty and Lily plan their walk to the bus stop.

items.example: If you need help, I will come.
items.note: Start with 'If you need help' to tell a friend you are ready whenever there is a problem.

items.example: If it rains, we will take an umbrella.
items.note: Say 'If it rains' to talk about possible rainy weather later.

items.example: If you hurry, you will not be late.
items.note: Say 'If you hurry' when someone needs to move quickly.

items.example: If you run to the station, you will catch it.
items.note: Use 'you will catch it' for a bus, train, or ball when you get there in time.

items.example: If you are late, I will wait at the door.
items.note: Say 'I will wait' to promise you will stay until your friend arrives.

items.example: Do not worry, I will help you.
items.note: Say 'Do not worry' to help a worried friend feel calm.

grammar.title: First conditional: If + present, will + verb
grammar.explanation: Use If + present tense for a real possibility, and will + base verb for what will happen next. Notice we do not put will after If.
examples: If you hurry, you will catch it.
If it rains, I will wait inside.
If you need help, I will help you.

practice.prompt: The bus leaves in two minutes! Which sentence makes sense?
practice.answer: If you hurry, you will catch it.
options: If you hurry, you will catch it.
If it rains, you will catch it.
If you sleep, you will catch it.
practice.explanation: Moving fast ('If you hurry') helps you catch the bus.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: If it rains, I will wait at the station.
practice.answer: If it rains, I will wait at the station.
options: If it rains, I will wait at the station.
If you hurry, I will wait at the park.
If you need help, I will call you.
practice.explanation: 'If it rains' talks about possible rain; 'I will wait' is the plan.

practice.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.
practice.explanation: Combine the 'If' condition with the right result.

practice.prompt: Tell your friend you are ready to help. Build the sentence.
practice.answer: If you need help I will wait.
practice.explanation: Use 'If you need help' + 'I will wait'.

practice.prompt: Look at the cloudy sky. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: If it ___, our shirts outside will get dirty.
practice.explanation: After 'If', use the present simple 'rains', not 'will rain'.

practice.prompt: Your friend is late and nervous. Comfort them.
practice.text: Do not ___, I will wait for you.
practice.explanation: 'Do not worry' tells someone to stay calm.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: Do not worry. If you hurry, you will catch it.
practice.answer: Do not worry. If you hurry, you will catch it.
practice.explanation: Use 'If you hurry, you will catch it' to encourage a friend.

lessons.title: Thank you and sorry
lessons.scenario: Tom drops a bucket of water in the laundry room and Mia helps him clean it up.

items.example: You found my wallet! Thank you so much!
items.note: Say 'Thank you so much' when someone gives you big help.

items.example: You carried my big box. That is very kind.
items.note: Say 'That is very kind' to praise a friend who helps you.

items.example: Thank you for helping me! — No problem!
items.note: Say 'No problem' as a friendly answer when someone thanks you or says sorry.

items.example: I forgot the pen! — Never mind, I have two.
items.note: Say 'Never mind' to tell someone not to worry about a small mistake.

items.example: I am so sorry I am late!
items.note: Say 'I am so sorry' when you feel bad about a mistake or problem.

items.example: I turned the wrong tap. It was my mistake.
items.note: Say 'It was my mistake' when you want to admit you did something wrong.

practice.prompt: Your friend fixed your broken lock. How do you thank them warmly?
practice.explanation: 'Thank you so much' shows strong thanks for helpful actions.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I am so sorry. It was my mistake.
practice.answer: I am so sorry. It was my mistake.
options: I am so sorry. It was my mistake.
Thank you so much. That is very kind.
practice.explanation: Use 'I am so sorry' and 'It was my mistake' to apologize.

practice.prompt: Match what one person says with the best reply.

pairs.left: I will carry that for you.
I am so sorry I forgot!

practice.explanation: Match each thank-you or apology with its natural response.

story.hook: What mistake does Tom make in the laundry room?

image.describe: Tom looking apologetic next to a tipped bucket of water in the laundry room while Smarty the black cat and Mia bring a mop.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Oh no! I am so sorry, Mia! Water from the bucket is everywhere!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Do not worry, Tom. What happened?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I walked too fast and hit the bucket. It was my mistake.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Never mind! Let me help. I will get the mop.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And I will bring a clean towel!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you so much, Mia and Smarty! That is very kind.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No problem, Tom! Friends always help.

story.hook: How do Smarty, Sam, and Mia get the stuck washing machine door open?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat, Sam, and Mia celebrating in front of the working washing machine in the tidy laundry room.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Mia, I have a problem! The washing machine stopped, and the door is stuck!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I am worried because my white shirt is inside! Could you give me a hand, Smarty?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Do not worry! If we turn it off and wait a moment, the lock will open.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Shall I call someone if it does not open?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes. Now wait five seconds… and let me help! I will open it.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Look, it opened! Problem solved! We did it!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thanks a lot, Smarty! That is very kind.

questions.prompt: What was stuck in the story?
questions.explanation: Sam says: The washing machine stopped, and the door is stuck!

questions.prompt: How did Smarty solve the problem?
questions.answer: He turned the machine off and waited a moment.
options: He turned the machine off and waited a moment.
He cleaned the door with a mop.
questions.explanation: Smarty said: If we turn it off and wait a moment, the lock will open.

questions.prompt: What do Mia and Sam say at the end?
questions.answer: Problem solved! We did it! Thanks a lot!
options: Problem solved! We did it! Thanks a lot!
I am so sorry! It was my mistake!
I lost my wallet! I am late!
questions.explanation: Mia celebrates with 'Problem solved! We did it!' and Sam says 'Thanks a lot, Smarty!'
